'''George James Doundoulakis''' (October 18, 1921 – March 17, 2007) was a [[Greek American]] [[physicist]] and soldier who worked under [[British intelligence agencies|British Intelligence]] during [[World War II]] with [[Special Operations Executive|SOE]] agent [[Patrick Leigh Fermor]], and then served with the [[Office of Strategic Services|OSS]] in [[Thessaly]], [[Greece]].

He is known for his twenty-six US patents in the fields of [[radar]], [[electronics]], and [[Narrow-bandwidth television|narrowband television]]. Doundoulakis is best remembered for the idea of suspending the [[antenna feed]] of the [[Arecibo radio telescope]] by cables and towers, eventually patented by his brother [[Helias Doundoulakis]].

A decorated veteran of [[World War II]], Doundoulakis formed an underground resistance organization in Crete under the [[Special Operations Executive]]. He escaped to Egypt and joined the [[U.S. Army]] and [[Office of Strategic Services]] – the OSS. He was sent back to Greece, where he outfitted and unified a [[communist|leftist]] rebel army, and was awarded the [[Legion of Merit]] from the [[United States Army]] and the [[King's Medal for Courage in the Cause of Freedom]] from [[Great Britain]].

==Early life==
George Doundoulakis was born in [[Detroit]], [[Michigan]] to Greek-immigrant parents, Demetrios and Evanthia (née Psaroudakis) Doundoulakis. When he was four years old, his family immigrated to [[Crete, Greece]] to look after their blind grandmother in the village of [[Archanes]]. Nearby was the [[Minoan civilization|Minoan]] excavations at [[Knossos]], where British archaeologist – later, SOE agent – [[John Pendlebury]] had been the curator.

By 1941, Greece had fallen to the [[Axis powers]] except [[Crete]]. On May 20, 1941, German [[paratrooper]]s invaded the island, known as the [[Battle of Crete]].

==World War II==

===Battle of Crete and the Cretan resistance===
During the [[Battle of Crete]], Doundoulakis assisted the Greek and British army headquarters in [[Archanes]], translating communiqués from other military posts.<ref name="Xlibris-2014" />{{RP|23}} After the British had been defeated, those soldiers who could not be evacuated either surrendered or went into hiding.

===Special Operations Executive===
[[Montague Woodhouse, 5th Baron Terrington|Montague Woodhouse]] was appointed [[Special Operations Executive|SOE]] chief on Crete, replacing [[John Pendlebury]], who had been executed by the Germans during the battle. Woodhouse approached Doundoulakis after spotting his savoir-faire as the Greek interpreter in Archanes. He requested that Doundoulakis support the SOE in hiding and evacuating British soldiers who had been left behind on Crete, with full knowledge that his efforts were punishable by death. Undaunted, Doundoulakis formed an underground organization under the command of the SOE's "Monty" Woodhouse. This would become one of the first [[Cretan resistance]] groups.<ref name="Beevor-1994">{{cite book |last1=Beevor |first1=Antony |title=Crete: The Battle And The Resistance |date=1994 |publisher=Westview Press |isbn=9780813320809 |edition=2nd }}</ref>{{RP|278}}<ref name="Kiriakopoulos-1995">{{cite book |last1=Kiriakopoulos |first1=G. C. |title=The Nazi Occupation of Crete, 1941-1945 |date=1995 |publisher=Praeger |isbn=9780275952778 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gjJnAAAAMAAJ |access-date=20 November 2020}}</ref>{{RP|190}}
Along with his brother [[Helias Doundoulakis]] and friends, they began scouring the island for recruits. Gathering momentum, Doundoulakis rounded up ex-military personnel and civilians from [[Heraklion]] and [[Lasithi]]. After Woodhouse left Crete, the SOE replaced him with [[Thomas Dunbabin|"Tom" Dunbabin]]. Risky sabotages under his watch were performed, such as the destruction of the [[Kastelli, Heraklion|Kastelli]] Airfield.<ref name="Xlibris-2014">{{cite book |last1=Doundoulakis |first1=Helias |last2=Gafni |first2=Gabriella |title=Trained to be an OSS Spy |date=2014 |publisher=Xlibris |isbn=9781499059830 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vkGtBAAAQBAJ |access-date=20 November 2020}}</ref>{{RP|33}} Along with friend [[Kimon Zografakis]] and two British commandos, Doundoulakis was able to set the airfield on fire after they placed explosives on seven German airplanes and hundreds of barrels of aviation fuel.<ref name="Beevor-1994" />{{RP|285}}<ref>{{cite AV media | people =William Stanley Moss, Patrick Leigh Fermor | title =The 11th Day: Crete 1941 | medium =Film | publisher =Archangel Films | location =Crete | year =2005 | url =http://www.the11thday.org/ | access-date =May 3, 2018 | archive-date =October 7, 2013 | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20131007131525/http://www.the11thday.org/ | url-status =dead }}</ref> Informants also uncovered German naval intelligence through a paramour of a German officer. After being relayed to Dunbabin, it resulted in the destruction of a German convoy destined to resupply Field Marshal [[Erwin Rommel]] and his [[Afrika Korps]] in September 1942. After the war, Doundoulakis was awarded the [[King's Medal for Courage in the Cause of Freedom]] from Great Britain for his services.<ref name="Xlibris-2014" />{{RP|33}} [[Thomas Dunbabin]] was awarded the [[Distinguished Service Order]] by the British military.<ref>Ogden, Alan. ''Sons of Odysseus: SOE Heroes in Greece'', Ch. 19, Bene Factum Publishing Ltd, 2013</ref>

Dunbabin finally left, and the SOE followed him up with the legendary [[Patrick Leigh Fermor]], known to the Cretans as "Mihalis".<ref name="Xlibris-2014" />{{RP|33}} George's intelligence circle grew exponentially. George and Leigh Fermor, along with guerrilla leader Manolis Bandouvas, would take refuge within the mountainous SOE hideouts of [[Mount Ida]].<ref name="Kiriakopoulos-1995" />{{RP|134}}<ref name="Xlibris-2014" />{{RP|37}}

After serving under the SOE for two years, Doundoulakis' ever-widening organization became apparent. He was blackmailed by a local Cretan who demanded one million drachmas as hush money. Otherwise, his organization and the SOE's Leigh Fermor would be let known to the Germans. Refusing the blackmail, Doundoulakis sent high school friends Sifis Migadis and John Androulakis to dispose of the traitor. However, they were too late in stopping the betrayal to the Gestapo. 
Leigh Fermor urged Doundoulakis to take flight at once to Crete's southern shore, and await evacuation by the SOE. They escaped through [[Mount Ida]] and the mountain ranges of [[Rethymno]] with others in his organization. After hiding in caves for a month, they were rescued by a British torpedo boat south of [[Tympaki|Tymbaki]].<ref>{{Citation | last =Doundoulakis | first =Helias | author-link =Helias Doundoulakis | title =I was Trained to be a Spy-Book II | place =Bloomington, IN | publisher =Xlibris | year =2012 | chapter =2 | chapter-url =https://books.google.com/books?id=0nUFBgAAQBAJ&q=timbaki | page =30 | language =English | isbn =978-1479716494}}</ref><ref name="Xlibris-2014" />{{RP|65}} Along with thirteen other resistance members, they headed to [[Mersa Matruh]], Egypt. As they were about to board, Doundoulakis reunited with Leigh Fermor and partisan leader [[Georgios Petrakis|Petrakogiorgis]]. Petrakogiorgis had returned to Crete on the same vessel carrying the Doundoulakis brothers to Egypt on June 7, 1943. They would not see Leigh Fermor for another forty years. [[Patrick Leigh Fermor|Leigh Fermor]] and [[W. Stanley Moss|"Billy" Stanley Moss]] became renowned after the war in the British book and film, [[Ill Met by Moonlight (film)|''Ill Met by Moonlight'']], for their [[Kidnap of Heinrich Kreipe|abduction of German General Kreipe]] from Crete. After reaching Mersa Matruh, Doundoulakis and his brother, as well as his close circle of friends, were transported to an SOE villa in [[Heliopolis, Cairo|Heliopolis]]. They were destined for SOE saboteur training upon the entreaty of [[Patrick Leigh Fermor|Leigh Fermor]], while the other escapees went off to the exiled [[Greek Armed Forces in the Middle East|Greek Army in the Middle East]].
Before leaving Crete, Doundoulakis instructed Mikis Akoumianakis to assume command of the organization that he had begun.<ref name="Xlibris-2014" />{{RP|52}}
Mikis Akoumianakis "took over the Allied intelligence network in Heraklion and became the key British agent in the region for the last three years of the war."<ref>{{cite book
 | last =Leigh Fermor
 | first =Patrick
 | author-link =Patrick Leigh Fermor
 | title =Abducting a General: the Kreipe Operation in Crete
 | chapter =2
 | chapter-url =https://books.google.com/books?id=BnKWBgAAQBAJ&q=akoumianakis
 | page =12
 | publisher =New York Review Books
 | date =2014
 | location =New York
 | language =English
 | isbn =9781590179383
 }}</ref> Later, along with [[Patrick Leigh Fermor|Leigh Fermor]] and [[W. Stanley Moss|"Billy" Moss]], he would become a key player in the [[kidnap of General Kreipe]] from Crete.<ref>{{Citation
 | last =Beevor
 | first =Antony
 | author-link =Antony Beevor
 | title =Crete: The Battle and the Resistance
 | place =Boulder, CO
 | publisher =Westview Press
 | year =1994
 | chapter =15: Stalemate at Rethymno and Heraklion
 | page =179
 | language =English
 | url =https://books.google.com/books?id=bZ47AgAAQBAJ&q=mikis+akoumianakis%3D
 | isbn =0-8133-2080-1
}}</ref>

===Office of Strategic Services (OSS)===
Two months of training at the lavish SOE villa in Heliopolis, Cairo, came to an abrupt end when Doundoulakis learned of the [[Office of Strategic Services]], the OSS. Doundoulakis contacted the fledgling American spy service that would become a key player in the Doundoulakis brothers' future. With help from Leigh Fermor, he informed the SOE commander of his intentions to join the [[American Army]]. Much to the SOE's dismay, George and Helias ultimately departed as comrades-in-arms and with hopes of defeating their common enemy.
 
The OSS dispatched Captain James Kellis to enlist the Doundoulakis brothers into the US Army on September 16, 1943, and were assigned to the OSS.<ref>{{cite book
 | last =Smith
 | first =Richard H.
 | title =OSS: The Secret History of America's First Central Intelligence Agency
 | page =258
 | chapter =8
 | chapter-url= https://books.google.com/books?id=83aMqklUijYC&q=james+kellis
 | publisher =Lyons Press
 | date =2005
 | location =Guilford, CT
 | language =English
 | isbn =1592287298
 }}</ref> Their Commanding Officer was Major [[John Vassos]], [[RCA Corporation|RCA]]'s eminent industrial designer. Agents were trained inside a secluded palace of [[King Farouk]]'s situated along [[Cairo, Egypt|Cairo's]] [[Nile River]], known as Ras el Kanayas.<ref>{{Citation
 | last =Hueck Allen
 | first =Susan
 | title =Classical Spies: American Archaeologists with the OSS in World War II Greece
 | place =Ann Arbor, Michigan
 | publisher =The University of Michigan
 | year =2013
 | chapter =7
 | chapter-url =https://books.google.com/books?id=jJZFDwAAQBAJ&q=ras+el+kanayas&pg=PT420
 | page =134
 | language =English
 | isbn =978-0472117697
}}</ref> Doundoulakis was trained in the [[Morale Operations Branch|Morale Operations]] (MO) and [[Special Operations]] (SO) branches.<ref name=Chambers-2008>{{cite book | last =Chambers II
 | first =John Whiteclay | title =OSS Training in the National Parks and Service Abroad in World War II |publisher =U.S. National Park Service | date =2008 | location =Washington, DC| isbn =978-1511654760 }}</ref>{{RP|40}}<ref name="Xlibris-2014" />{{RP|136}}

[[Special Operations]] was modeled after the SOE, which included parachute, sabotage, defensive, weapons, and leadership training to support guerrilla or partisan resistance. [[Morale Operations Branch|Morale Operations]] training included psychological warfare and propaganda.<ref name="Chambers-2008" />{{RP|40,43}} After his training, Doundoulakis was sent to the port city of [[Volos, Greece]] in [[Thessaly]]. His mission, known as "Horsebreeders," was to coordinate some 7,000 Greek [[Greek People's Liberation Army|leftist rebels]] into a unified fighting force.<ref>{{Citation
 | last =Hueck Allen
 | first =Susan
 | title =Classical Spies: American Archaeologists with the OSS in World War II Greece
 | place =Ann Arbor, Michigan
 | publisher =The University of Michigan
 | year =2013
 | chapter =11
 | chapter-url =https://books.google.com/books?id=jJZFDwAAQBAJ&q=volos
 | page =391
 | language =English
 | isbn =978-0472117697
}}</ref> Doundoulakis provided the necessary logistic sustainment that included weapons, a printing press, clothing, and materials for his secret army through OSS bases in Turkey. He had printed and distributed leaflets intended for German soldiers and Greek collaborators, to subvert their confidence while encouraging the Greek population to resist. They were able to inflict enough damage to Volos' railroad transportation hub and its maritime shipping, that it contributed to the demise of the German supply line near Athens. The Germans were unable to remove Doundoulakis and the [[Greek People's Liberation Army|leftist rebels]] hidden in the impassable [[Pelion]] Mountains. Unrelenting attacks upon German communications and railway links led to an overwhelming success. Doundoulakis was promoted to first sergeant and awarded the [[Legion of Merit]] in OSS-Cairo.<ref>{{Citation
 | last =Hueck Allen
 | first =Susan
 | title =Classical Spies: American Archaeologists with the OSS in World War II Greece
 | place =Ann Arbor, Michigan
 | publisher =The University of Michigan
 | year =2013
 | chapter =13
 | chapter-url =https://books.google.com/books?id=jJZFDwAAQBAJ&q=george+doundoulakis&pg=PP1
 | page =391
 | language =English
 | isbn =978-0472117697
}}</ref><ref name="Xlibris-2014" />{{RP|295}}

His brother, [[Helias Doundoulakis]], was trained at Cairo's [[Camp X]]-type 'Spy School' where he was sent on a mission to [[Thessaloniki, Greece|Salonica, Greece]].<ref name="Chambers-2008" />{{RP|50}} There, Helias set up a fake business from a bombed-out factory once owned by [[Greek Jews]] who had fled from Nazi persecution. He remained embedded in Salonica from April to December 1944, sending encrypted radio messages to OSS-Cairo on German troop movements.<ref>{{cite AV media
 | people =William J. Donovan, William Fairbairn, William Stephenson, Frank Gleason, Guy D'Artois, Helias Doundoulakis
 | title =World War II Spy School
 | medium =Film
 | publisher =YAP Films
 | location =USA, Canada
 | date =2014
 | url =https://www.smithsonianchannel.com/videos/how-to-lie-for-your-life/34349
 | access-date =August 13, 2018
 | archive-date =July 13, 2018
 | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20180713202551/https://www.smithsonianchannel.com/videos/how-to-lie-for-your-life/34349
 | url-status =dead
 }}</ref><ref name="Kiriakopoulos-1995" />{{RP|190}}

==Post-war==
Doundoulakis spent the remainder of his enlistment at the [[Congressional Country Club]] in [[Bethesda, MD]], which had been commandeered by [[William J. Donovan|"Wild Bill" Donovan's]] [[Office of Strategic Services|OSS]] as a training ground known by its codename "[[Congressional Country Club|Area F]]".<ref name="Chambers-2008" />{{RP|195-199}} Following his discharge, Doundoulakis settled in [[Brooklyn, NY]].

===Education===
After settling in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York (state)|New York]], Doundoulakis received a bachelor's degree in physics from [[New York University Tandon School of Engineering|Brooklyn Polytechnic]] in 1953 under the [[GI Bill]]. He went on to earn his Master of Science in physics at [[New York University Tandon School of Engineering|Brooklyn Polytechnic]] under renowned physicist and X-ray crystallographer [[Paul Peter Ewald]] in 1955.

===RCA Institutes===
After receiving his master's of physics from Brooklyn Polytechnic, Doundoulakis found his metier in electronics, radio physics and the advancing field of radar and television. Tutored by Ira Kamen, one of the preeminent electrical engineers in New York City at the [[TCI College of Technology|RCA Institutes]], Doundoulakis gained a solid foothold in the field. Subsequently, he taught electronics at the RCA Institutes. In 1956, Doundoulakis and Ira Kamen filed their first US patent.<ref>{{cite patent
 | inventor1-last = Doundoulakis
 | inventor1-first = George
 | inventor2-last = Kamen
 | inventor2-first = Ira
 | title = Feed system for broadband antenna
 | issue-date = 1961
 | patent-number = 2989748
 | country-code = US }}</ref>

===General Bronze Corporation===
Seeing the potential of this rising star in a rapidly developing field, Doundoulakis was hired by the [[General Bronze Corporation]] in [[Garden City, New York]] as head of [[Research and Development]] (R&D). At the time, General Bronze was dedicated to pioneering and taking the lead in the commercial market of antenna designs. Along with Stanley Gethin, he copyrighted antenna and radar-related projects for General Bronze.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Doundoulakis |first1=George |last2=Gethin |first2=Stanley |title=Catalog of Copyright Entries |entry=Design considerations on modern scatter systems. |series= 3 |volume=13 |issue=1 |page=194 |publisher=US Copyright Office |place=Library of Congress |date=1958 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TSEhAQAAIAAJ&q=george+doundoulakis&pg=PA194}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Doundoulakis |first1=George |last2=Gethin |first2=Stanley |title=Catalog of Copyright Entries |entry=Far field patterns of parabaloidal reflectors. |series= 3 |volume=13 |issue=1 |page=194 |publisher=US Copyright Office |place=Library of Congress |date=1958 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TSEhAQAAIAAJ&q=george+doundoulakis&pg=PA194}}</ref>

===Arecibo Radio Telescope===
As the head of Research and Development for General Bronze, Doundoulakis was notified by [[Cornell University]] of their intent to build a [[Arecibo Radio Telescope|radio telescope]]. Subsequently, he was invited to Cornell the day the project for the design and construction of the antenna at [[Arecibo, Puerto Rico]] was announced, by Professor [[William E. Gordon|William Gordon]]. Gordon, who led the project for Cornell, indicated at that time that the support for the [[antenna feed]] – or "eye" – was envisioned to be a 500-foot tower situated in the center of the 1000&nbsp;ft. reflector.<ref>{{Citation| last = Gordon| first = William| author-link = William E. Gordon| title = Cornell will build a radar to observe the ionosphere| newspaper = New York Herald Tribune
| location = New York City| type = Engineer's News Supplement| date = October 25, 1959| page = 1}}</ref><ref>{{cite book| first1 =William E. | last1 =Gordon | author-link =William E. Gordon
| first2 =Henry | last2 =Booker | author2-link =Henry G. Booker | first3 =Ben | last3 =Nichols | chapter =Design Study of a Radar to Explore the Earth's Ionosphere and Surrounding Space
| title=Research Report EE 395 | series =3 | year =1958 | pages =23 | place =Ithaca, New York | publisher =Cornell University, School of Electrical Engineering }}</ref><ref>{{Citation
| last =Matthews | first =John | title =A short history of geophysical radar at Arecibo Observatory | journal =History of Geo- and Space Sciences | volume =4 | issue =1 | page =20
| publisher = Copernicus Publications | year =2013 | url =https://www.hist-geo-space-sci.net/4/19/2013/hgss-4-19-2013.pdf | doi =10.5194/hgss-4-19-2013 | bibcode =2013HGSS....4...19M | doi-access =free }}</ref>

Doundoulakis, foreseeing a simpler approach with a suspended [[antenna feed]], leapt at the opportunity. Along with Zachary Sears – who directed Internal Design at Digital B & E Corporation of New York – he received the [[request for proposal]] (RFP) from [[Cornell University]] for the antenna design. He studied the idea of suspending the [[antenna feed]] with his brother, [[Helias Doundoulakis]], a civil engineer who was then working for [[Emery Roth]]. Doundoulakis identified the problem that a tower or tripod would have presented around the center, which is the most critical portion of the reflector. Instead, Doundoulakis' proposal of a revolutionary design, by suspending the [[antenna feed|feed]] from cables connected to towers, was more practical. Rather than having a massive tower in the center of the reflector, his design would save millions in construction costs.<ref>{{Citation| last = Frè| first = Pietro|year = 2013| title = Gravity, a geometrical course| chapter = 7| chapter-url = https://books.google.com/books?id=1klJvLbHEQYC&q=radio+telescope+suspension+system&pg=PA276| edition = 1| volume = 1:Development of the theory and basic physical applications| publisher = Springer| location = New York| page = 276| isbn = 978-94-007-5360-0| doi = 10.1007/978-94-007-5361-7| bibcode = 2013ggc1.book.....F}}</ref><ref>{{Citation
| last = Gold| first = Thomas| author-link = Thomas Gold|year = 2013| title = Taking the Back off the Watch: A Personal Memoir| volume = 381| chapter = 7| chapter-url = https://books.google.com/books?id=vlaFA0zgmSoC&q=gordon| edition = 1| publisher = Springer Heidelberg| location = New York| page = 119| isbn = 978-3-642-27587-6| url = https://books.google.com/books?id=vlaFA0zgmSoC&q=Gordon+| doi = 10.1007/978-3-642-27588-3| series = Astrophysics and Space Science Library| url-access = subscription}}</ref>

He presented his proposal to Cornell University for a suspension system of the [[antenna feed|feed]]. This suspension system would possess a doughnut or [[torus]]-type [[truss]] suspended by four cables from four towers, to provide along its edge a rail track intended for [[azimuth]]al positioning of the [[antenna feed|feed]]. A second [[truss]] in the form of an [[arch]] was to hang below and rotate on said rails through 360 degrees. The arch also provided rails onto which the unit supporting the feed would move to provide for the elevational positioning of the feed. A counter-weight would move symmetrically opposite to the feed position for overall stability. George informed his brother, [[Helias Doundoulakis]], to design the cable suspension system which was finally adopted for the Arecibo Antenna. A patent was filed on September 11, 1961, by [[Helias Doundoulakis]] for "A radio telescope having a scanning feed supported by a cable suspension over a stationary reflector"<ref>{{US patent reference| number = 3273156| y = 1966| m = 09| d = 13| inventor = Helias Doundoulakis| title = Radio Telescope having a scanning feed supported by a cable suspension over a stationary reflector}}</ref> who designed the suspension system according to George's specifications. Although the present configuration of the Arecibo Antenna is identical to the original drawings by George and Helias Doundoulakis (except with three towers, instead of the four towers drawn in Doundoulakis' patent<ref>{{Citation| last =Cohen| first =Marshall H.| year =2009| title =Genesis of the 1000-foot Arecibo dish| journal =Journal of Astronomical History and Heritage| volume =12| issue =2| pages =141–152| doi =10.3724/SP.J.1440-2807.2009.02.06| url =http://www.narit.or.th/en/files/2009JAHHvol12/2009JAHH...12..141C.pdf| bibcode =2009JAHH...12..141C| s2cid =18990068| access-date =May 5, 2018| archive-date =August 20, 2018| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20180820141251/http://www.narit.or.th/en/files/2009JAHHvol12/2009JAHH...12..141C.pdf| url-status =dead}}</ref>), the [[United States Patent and Trademark Office]] finally granted [[Helias Doundoulakis]] a U.S. patent on September 13, 1966 – for designing the radio telescope's suspension system.<ref>{{cite patent | inventor1-last = Doundoulakis | inventor1-first = Helias
| title = Radio telescope having a scanning feed supported by a cable suspension over a stationary reflector | issue-date = 1966 | patent-number = 3273156 | country-code = US }}</ref> 
Two other assignees on the patent were close friends [[William J. Casey]], ex-director of the [[CIA]] under [[President Reagan]], and attorney Constantine Michalos.

After the observatory was damaged by [[Hurricane Maria]] in 2017, it was also affected by earthquakes in 2019 and 2020. Two cable breaks, one in August 2020 and a second in November 2020, threatened the structural integrity of the support structure for the suspended platform and damaged the dish. Due to uncertainty over the remaining strength of the other cables supporting the suspended structure, and the risk of collapse due to further failures making repairs dangerous, the NSF announced on November 19, 2020, that it would decommission and dismantle the telescope.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clery |first=Daniel |date=November 19, 2020 |title=Famed Arecibo telescope, on the brink of collapse, will be dismantled |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/famed-arecibo-telescope-brink-collapse-will-be-dismantled|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201119163508/https://www.sciencemag.org/news/2020/11/famed-arecibo-telescope-brink-collapse-will-be-dismantled|archive-date=November 19, 2020|access-date=November 19, 2020 |website=Science {{!}} AAAS|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Witze |first=Alexandra |date=November 19, 2020 |title=Legendary Arecibo telescope will close forever – scientists are reeling |journal=Nature |volume=587 |issue=7835 |pages=529–530 |language=en |doi=10.1038/d41586-020-03270-9|pmid=33214727 |bibcode=2020Natur.587..529W |doi-access= }}</ref> Before it could be decommissioned, several of the remaining support cables suffered a critical failure and the support structure, antenna, and dome assembly all fell into the dish at 7:55&nbsp;a.m. local time on December 1, 2020, destroying the telescope.<ref name="guardian collapsed">{{cite news |title=Giant Arecibo radio telescope collapses in Puerto Rico |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/dec/01/arecibo-radio-telescope-collapses-puerto-rico |access-date=1 December 2020 |work=[[The Guardian]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=1 December 2020}}</ref><ref name="ap collapse">{{cite news | url = https://apnews.com/article/puerto-rico-0da6abb251f455977bf0c752348e712e | title = Huge Puerto Rico radio telescope, already damaged, collapses | first = DÁNICA | last = Coto | date = December 1, 2020 | access-date = December 1, 2020 | work = [[Associated Press]] |via=[[Yahoo!]]}}</ref>

===Advancement Devices and William J. Casey===

In the 1950s, Doundoulakis began his own company dedicated to pursuing his patent designs and applying them to the market. Advancement Devices was launched, through which [[William J. Casey]] first heard of the inventor. In WWII, Casey had been chief of the OSS' Secret Intelligence branch for Europe.<ref name="Persico-1990">{{cite book |last1=Persico |first1=Joseph E. |title=Casey: From the OSS to the CIA |date=1990 |publisher=Viking |isbn=9780670823420 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3CeGAAAAMAAJ |access-date=20 November 2020}}</ref>{{RP|68}} He learned that Doundoulakis also served in the OSS, and had secured a contract from the "[[Signal Corps (United States Army)|Army Signal Corps]] to produce a radar that could measure the trajectory of a mortar shell. But he lacked the capital to follow through on his bid."<ref name="Persico-1990" />{{RP|101}} Following this lead, Casey ensured that all the necessary funding would accompany Doundoulakis' future projects. Under Advancement Devices, and with contributions from Casey, Doundoulakis developed a stream of patents for electronics, television, and internal ballistic engines.

One patent, the tri-rotor engine, became a matter of contention with the IRS in back taxes owed by Casey to the IRS.<ref>{{Citation | last =Babcock | first =Charles | title =CIA Director Disputes IRS Claim to $100,000 in Back Taxes | newspaper =The Washington Post | page =A3 | date =May 13, 1984 | url =https://www.cia.gov/library/readingroom/docs/CIA-RDP90-00965R000100270045-6.pdf| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20170123140854/https://www.cia.gov/library/readingroom/docs/CIA-RDP90-00965R000100270045-6.pdf| url-status =dead| archive-date =January 23, 2017}}</ref> Nonetheless, the Doundoulakis/Casey business partnership would beget a life-long friendship from, "the inventor who he had long subsidized."<ref name="Persico-1990" />{{RP|166}} Their bond was not only grounded in their prior service with the OSS but in an alliance that continued throughout Casey's Congressional hearings prior to his [[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission|SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission)]] post. Doundoulakis was called to testify before the [[United States Congress]] on Casey's behalf.<ref>{{Citation| year = 1970
| title = The Nomination of William J. Casey| journal = Securities Industry Study: Hearing[s], Ninety-second Congress, First [-second] Session | volume = 9 | issue = 1| publisher = U.S. Government Printing Office| location = Washington, DC| language = English| page = 744| url = https://books.google.com/books?id=wYNKAQAAIAAJ&q=george+doundoulakis+and+william+casey}}</ref> He eventually was sworn in and became head of the Securities and Exchange Commission under [[President Nixon]]. Afterward, under the [[presidency of Ronald Reagan]], Casey was appointed the director of the [[Central Intelligence Agency]].

==Personal life==
Doundoulakis married Chrysanthe "Chris" (Markomihalakis) in [[Brooklyn]], New York, where they settled after the war, resettling in [[North Bellmore, New York]]. They had two sons and one daughter, and three grandchildren.

During the 1980s, [[Patrick Leigh Fermor|Leigh Fermor]] visited and stayed with Doundoulakis at his North Bellmore home, during one of the many celebrations for the [[Battle of Crete]] and [[Kidnapping of Heinrich Kreipe|the abduction of Gen. Kreipe]], punctuating a friendship which had endured throughout both their lives.

==Death==
George Doundoulakis died on March 17, 2007, and was buried with military honors in Greenfield Cemetery, [[Uniondale, New York]].

==Awards==
* 2015 – Both George and Helias Doundoulakis were recipients of the OSS Society's 2015 Distinguished Service Award at the annual Donovan Award Dinner<ref>[http://www.osssociety.org/award.html annual Donovan Award Dinner]</ref> honoring [[Hugh Montgomery (diplomat)|Ambassador Hugh Montgomery]] in Washington, DC.<ref>{{Citation
 | last =Lamothe

 | title =Spy party: Tuxedos, martinis and some of the greatest heroes of World War II
 | newspaper =The Washington Post

 | url =https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/checkpoint/wp/2015/11/09/at-black-tie-affair-modern-spies-meet-spunky-nonagenarian-world-war-ii-heroes/
}}
</ref><ref>{{cite AV media
 | people =Amb. Hugh Montgomery, Frank Gleason, Peter Ortiz, Ernest Hemingway
 | title =Distinguished Service Award Presentation
 | medium =video
 | publisher =OSS Society
 | location =Washington, DC

* 2008 – OSS Society, May and November, Meritorious Service Award, by the Greek Government and OSS Society, Astoria, NY
* 1991 – PAA, [[Pancretan Association of America]] Distinguished Service Award, 50th Anniversary of Battle of Crete, Astoria, NY
